newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yields end slightly lower in subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ yields end slightly lower in subdued trade.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against Friday's close

* NZ debt markets close slightly firmer after quiet session
* Tuesday's Qtrly Employment Survey major focus for bills
* Bond market awaits Greenspan testimony later this week

A firmer New Zealand dollar helped short-term wholesale interest rates to close slightly lower on Monday, but trade was lacklustre and dealers said the market was waiting on Tuesday's Quarterly Employment Survey for direction.
"It's been a very quiet day. The market is just focusing on tomorrow's numbers and you possibly just saw a little bit of book squaring ahead of them," said one bill trader.
The 90-day bank bill yield edged a couple of points lower on the day, but was still very much stuck in a range.
"The market is just waiting for a reason to trade in a particular direction and break out of this 20 point range we've been in for the last month," the trader said.
Dealers said the November quarter QES, which measures wage pressures, was a critical release and certainly has the potential to move the market significantly.
Bankers Trust economists said the QES, due at 10.45 a.m. (2145 GMT) on Tuesday, may be the difference between the RBNZ holding the line or opting for an early monetary policy tightening.
BT expects a 0.7 percent rise in total ordinary time wages in the quarter for an annual rise of 3.5 percent.
In the bond market, the firmer Kiwi maintained a reasonable bid tone and rates closed a few points lower.
But trade was also subdued as the market awaits Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before the Senate and the House on February 26-27.
"For the fixed income market, that's definitely the focus, said one dealer, adding that a strong QES on Tuesday could also move bond rates.
